note: CENSUS OF COMMITTED THIRD-PARTY TREES. Every directory under vendor/ has exactly one row here and vice versa (exact complements — test/unit/dependency_integrity_tripwire.test.ts); a row may instead carry an explicit `root` (a tracked directory outside vendor/ and node_modules) for a tree that must live inside another self-contained subsystem, and scripts/lib/third_party_census.ts derives from the tree every committed file that looks third-party and requires it to lie under some row's root. FOUR AXES since 2026-09-04: the three below plus LICENCE — every row carries `licence: {spdx, file}`, an id from the closed set in scripts/vendor_verify.ts and a licence text INSIDE the tree that must read as that licence (OPS-08). A vendored lib has no lockfile line, no sha512- integrity, no registry and no Dependabot: tree_sha256 is the ONLY thing in this repo that hashes those bytes. Verify: bun run scripts/vendor_verify.ts. Bump: bun run scripts/vendor_fetch.ts --lib <id> --version <v> --url <archive> --sha256 <expected>. tree_sha256 = sha256 over the sorted concatenation of `<posix relpath>\0<sha256(file bytes)>\n` for every regular file under the lib root, so contents AND file set are covered. THREE AXES, and a row must satisfy all three. (1) INTEGRITY — tree_sha256/files, recomputed every run. (2) IDENTITY — version_evidence: the declared version must appear verbatim in a file of the lib's OWN tree, so the label cannot be moved without the bytes (a mislabelled row would otherwise satisfy the digest, the range check and the feed query at once). A tree that states no version anywhere says so in unprovable_reason. scripts/vendor_verify.ts --write REFUSES to bless a tree whose bytes do not state the declared version. (3) ADVISORIES + STALENESS — the `advisory` block: the coordinate a feed is keyed to, a per-row review window, and a LEDGER of the published advisories known to touch that version; `reviewed` is the ISO date a human last checked THIS lib's upstream release feed AND the advisory feed (Dependabot cannot watch a vendored tree). Since CLI-26 (2026-08-28) that date is GATED, not printed: test/unit/vendor_advisory_tripwire.test.ts hard-fails when the declared version is inside a ledgered range or when `reviewed` is past the window, and scripts/ci/audit.ts asks the GitHub advisory feed the same question when it can reach it, reds on anything this ledger does not already carry, and reports a lookup that did not complete as DEGRADED rather than as a finding. The rows added or re-blessed on 2026-09-04 (lz-string, swagger-ui, the licence files under ckeditor and json-view) carry that date; the three remaining original rows were reviewed on 2026-08-28 and carry that date: ckeditor5@42.0.1 (two moderate XSS advisories in range, both ledgered and accepted on re-proved clauses), pdfjs-dist@6.2.108 (feed returns nothing), and json-view, which no feed can be keyed to at all and whose review window is therefore its only signal. Moving a `reviewed` date is a claim that a human read both feeds — which is the one thing this field exists to make expensive. The fourth original row, xlsx (SheetJS 0.20.3), was REMOVED 2026-09-24 with its tree: tool_export builds XLSX/ODS server-side (tools/tool_export/server/writers/) and no client code loads SheetJS any more.

ckeditor.upstream: none — a bespoke Dédalo webpack build (ddEditor + the dedalo_image_tags and reference plugins); no upstream artifact exists to re-fetch
ckeditor.note: Not reproducible: the build project no longer exists in any checkout, and build/ckeditor.js.map is the only surviving copy of the plugin source — which is why the map is committed. Standing risk: the bundle can only be replaced wholesale, never patched. Reviewed 2026-08-28 against the GitHub advisory feed (ckeditor5@42.0.1): two moderate XSS advisories in range, both requiring General HTML Support — ledgered and accepted below on a clause this repo re-proves every run. LICENCE (OPS-08, 2026-09-04): the tree shipped no licence text; LICENSE.md is CKEditor 5's own v42.0.1 LICENSE.md (GPL-2.0-or-later, per the file's 'Licensed under the terms of GNU General Public License Version 2 or later' and the 'For licensing, see LICENSE.md' banner every served chunk carries). Adding it moved tree_sha256 (73 → 74 files); the bundle bytes are unchanged.

advisories.summary: CKEditor 5 has Cross-site Scripting (XSS) in the HTML Support package

accepted.reason: The advisory fires only where General HTML Support is enabled AND configured to accept unsafe markup. This bespoke build ships neither the GeneralHtmlSupport nor the HtmlEmbed plugin (0 hits each in the served bundle), so the configuration the advisory names cannot exist here. Not fixable by upgrade: the build project no longer exists in any checkout, so the bundle can only be replaced wholesale.

advisories.summary: Cross-site scripting (XSS) in the clipboard package

accepted.reason: The advisory requires the Block Toolbar plugin AND either General HTML Support with unsafe markup or HTML Embed. Neither GeneralHtmlSupport nor HtmlEmbed is in the served bundle, and service_ckeditor.js keeps htmlEmbed commented out of the toolbar. Refuted independently by the 2026-08-26 audit on three checks. Same wholesale-replacement constraint as the row above.

json-view.note: Distributed via GitHub/jsDelivr only, never published to npm. The bundle carries no version string, so the tree digest IS the identity of this copy. Reviewed 2026-08-28: no npm advisories can be keyed to it (never published there), no upstream release since the bundle was taken, last upstream commit 2025-12-03. LICENCE (OPS-08, 2026-09-04): the bundle shipped no licence text; LICENSE is the upstream repository's MIT text (pgrabovets/json-view, master). Adding it moved tree_sha256 (3 → 4 files); the bundle bytes are unchanged.

advisory.unkeyable_reason: The bundle carries no version string and pgrabovets/json-view was never published to npm, so there is no ecosystem+name+version coordinate any advisory feed can be keyed to. The tree digest IS the identity of this copy, and the review window below is the only staleness signal this row can carry — which is why it is short rather than absent.

version_evidence.unprovable_reason: The bundle carries no version string of any kind: jsonview.bundle.js is 6316 bytes and the word "version" does not occur in it, so there is no literal in these bytes that could evidence a declared version. That is also why the advisory coordinate is null. tree_sha256 IS the identity of this copy — it is the whole identity, not a corroboration of one — and the review window is the only staleness signal the row can carry.

pdfjs.note: The standalone viewer app (web/viewer.html), which npm's pdfjs-dist does not ship and bun cannot install (a .zip, not a .tgz). Bumped 2026-08-28 from 5.7.284 to 6.2.108 for GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j / CVE-2026-16633 (HIGH, arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a malicious PDF, >= 5.6.83 < 6.2.108); 6.2.108 is also the npm dist-tag latest, so this is the project's latest-stable law and the advisory fix in one move. archive_sha256 is now the FULL digest and it is the one GitHub publishes for the release asset (assets[].digest), not a prefix copied by hand — the previous row could only record 6d1b8125…, which is why it stayed null. Trimmed with scripts/vendor_fetch.ts --drop '**/*.map' --drop 'web/compressed.tracemonkey-pldi-09.pdf', so the tree never equals the archive and the trim is reproducible from the command line rather than done by hand. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 against a fresh download of the archive above (which hashes to archive_sha256): the archive holds 409 files, this tree holds 404, the 5 missing ones are exactly build/pdf.mjs.map, build/pdf.sandbox.mjs.map, build/pdf.worker.mjs.map, web/viewer.mjs.map (9,034,413 bytes together) and web/compressed.tracemonkey-pldi-09.pdf (1,016,315 bytes, and view_default_edit_pdf.js disables it anyway by clearing defaultUrl), and every one of the 404 files is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the archive's copy. 3.5 MB gzipped (3,694,821 bytes, per-file gzip -c summed). 404 files vs 401 before: the file set is otherwise identical to 5.7.284 — the three additions are signature-properties toolbar icons. The mount also forces enableScripting:false (client/dedalo/core/component_pdf/js/view_default_edit_pdf.js), which is the advisory's own stated workaround and holds even if this bump were ever reverted — but ONLY behind disablePreferences:true, set immediately before it: enableScripting is a PREFERENCE-kind option, so a stored pdfjs.preferences entry is applied over it after the mount's handler returns. Both facts are gated (test/unit/vendor_advisory_tripwire.test.ts), and the gate EXECUTES the vendored AppOptions implementation to prove the chain rather than grepping for the strings. DELIBERATELY KEPT: pdf.sandbox.mjs and web/wasm/quickjs-eval.wasm. With enableScripting:false they are never instantiated, and dropping them would make a future re-enable fail silently while diverging this tree from the upstream layout the digest documents — a trap for the next bump, not a control.

advisories.summary: PDF.js: Arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a malicious PDF. Ledgered after the fix on purpose: the row is inert at 6.2.108 and reds instantly if anyone takes this tree back below the patched version.

lz-string.note: URL-state compression for tool_common / component_text_area (compressToEncodedURIComponent). WHY VENDORED: lz-string ships UMD only — libs/lz-string.js declares a top-level `var LZString` and exports through define/module/angular; there is no ESM entry and no `module` field in any release up to 1.5.0. A classic <script> would make it a global; an ES module import cannot reach a module-scoped var, and this client is all modules — so the registry copy is unusable AS SERVED, which is VENDORING.md §1's fifth case. ONE DECLARED PATCH over the npm 1.5.0 dist: `var LZString = (function() {` → `export const LZString = (function() {` and the 11-line UMD tail removed; nothing else differs (diffed 2026-09-04 against the extracted archive, whose sha256 is archive_sha256). The patch is covered by tree_sha256 — the 'never patched in place' rule means never patched SILENTLY. Tree: lz-string.js (patched), LICENSE and package.json verbatim (the latter carries the only 1.5.0 literal — the bundle banner still says 'version 1.4.5', which upstream never bumped). Until P2-5-residue (CLI-12) a 1.4.5 copy with the same patch and a WTFPL banner lived at client/dedalo/core/common/js/utils/lzstring.js with no digest and no advisory watch; 1.5.0 is the npm dist-tag latest and is MIT. Reviewed 2026-09-04 against the GitHub advisory feed (lz-string@1.5.0): none.

swagger-ui.note: The Swagger UI page of the v1 PHP publication API (publication/server_api/v1/docu/ui/index.html). WHY NOT UNDER vendor/: the v1 tree is a self-contained Apache+PHP folder deployed on its own — it has no node_modules and no engine to serve /dedalo/lib/, and release_archive_tripwire refuses symlinks, so the bytes must sit inside that folder; the explicit `root` is what lets this manifest hash them there. Bumped 2026-09-04 (PUB-12) from 4.5.2 (2022-02-21, built from a dirty tree, 16 MB with every map and es bundle, no pin, no reason) to 5.32.14, the npm dist-tag latest. TRIMMED to what index.html loads plus the licence texts: swagger-ui-bundle.js, swagger-ui-standalone-preset.js, swagger-ui.css, the two favicons, LICENSE, NOTICE and the two *.LICENSE.txt. DROPPED: every .map, swagger-ui.js and the es bundles (nothing loads them), the upstream index.html/index.css/index.js/swagger-initializer.js/absolute-path.js/README/package.json/log.* (not served), and oauth2-redirect.html — its 5.x form loads oauth2-redirect.js and this API has no OAuth2 flow, so shipping the page without the script would be a broken page, and shipping both would be dead code. Every kept file is byte-identical to the archive's copy (archive_sha256 is the sha256 of the .tgz, verified on download). Reviewed 2026-09-04 against the GitHub advisory feed (swagger-ui-dist@5.32.14): none. Bumped 2026-10-24 to 5.34.0 (the npm dist-tag latest, the same release publication/server_api/v2 locks) with scripts/vendor_fetch.ts and the SAME nine-file trim; the .tgz matched the registry sha512 integrity (= the v2 bun.lock entry) before its sha256 was recorded. Reviewed 2026-10-24 against the GitHub advisory feed (swagger-ui-dist@5.34.0): none.

transformers.note: The in-browser AI runtime (transformers.js): tool_transcription's speech recognition, tool_lang's translation, the remove_background processor — served at /dedalo/lib/transformers/dist/transformers.js, the ONLY file of the package any client imports. WHY VENDORED (P1-23 / DEAD-12): the registry package is a Node-side bundle first. Its `dependencies` pull onnxruntime-node (211 MB of native binaries, unpacked at install by adm-zip) and sharp/@img (16 MB of libvips) into every `bun install --production` of every installation and of every code-update quarantine, while the engine imports NONE of it — no src/tools/publication module names @huggingface/transformers; the sole consumer is the browser, through the client-lib registry. That native closure was also the ONLY path to two of the three HIGH entries the advisory baseline accepted (adm-zip, sharp). A browser-only bundle has no install-time Node dependency at all, so it is committed like any other served third-party tree: 1.28 MB gitignored-nowhere, digest-pinned, feed-watched, and the 567 MB stops shipping. The bundle is self-contained esbuild output (no relative imports): it fetches its onnxruntime-web WASM glue from env.backends.onnx.wasm.wasmPaths, which every importer pins to /dedalo/lib/onnxruntime/dist/ (no_remote_code_tripwire), served from the explicit onnxruntime-web npm pin — the registry `onnxruntime` row. THAT PIN AND THIS BUNDLE ARE ONE DEPENDENCY: the bundle compiles in onnxruntime-web's JS core and loads the .mjs/.wasm glue through wasmPaths, so the pin is exactly the onnxruntime-web build this release declares and was built and tested against (4.3.0 → 1.31.0-dev.20260914-8d85527a0), dev label and all — the served pair is the upstream-tested pair, not a combination nobody tested. (Mismatched pairs have run: 4.2.0's 1.26.0-dev core over 1.29.0 and over 1.30.0 glue both produced bit-identical outputs, measured 2026-10-04 in a clean browser context. That is evidence they CAN work, not that any future pair will.) onnxruntime_alignment_tripwire holds bundle = package.json = bun.lock, so a lone onnxruntime-web bump is red until it arrives with a re-vendor of this tree. Trimmed with --strip 1 --keep dist/transformers.js --keep LICENSE: dropped transformers.min.js / .web(.min).js (nothing imports them; switching the client to the .min build is a separate change), every transformers.node.* build (Node-side, never served), dist/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.mjs (referenced by no string in the kept bundle — its loader resolves the .asyncify glue through wasmPaths), src/, types/, README.md, package.json. Byte-verified 2026-10-04: the kept transformers.js is identical (cmp) to dist/transformers.js of the 4.3.0 registry tarball, and the archive's sha512 equals the registry's published `integrity` (sha512-fL1A/WUZwouP…) — archive_sha256 is the sha256 of that verified archive, since the registry publishes sha512 and vendor_fetch records sha256. Reviewed 2026-10-04 against the GitHub advisory feed (@huggingface/transformers@4.3.0 and onnxruntime-web@1.31.0-dev.20260914-8d85527a0): none.
